rows: Technique. Sure. Show me one you have used on somebody who was trying to stop you.
I brawl. I have never needed a speech to prove it.
Risk gets people hurt. I take it when I have no other option.
Time, to me, is fine. Heavy is better.
The crowd came to see work. They will get work.
I am not here to be liked.
Respect is earned in the ring. I do not need anybody to tell me I have it.
Look at the stance. Hot, ready. This is how I stand when I am ready to go.
Technique, that word. Prove it, then. I will be waiting.
Strikes come first and the rest follows. You will know when you have taken one.
The gamble is only worth it if the outcome is worth it. Yours is not.
Stalling is an admission. I do not stall.
The people want a contest, not a press conference. Let them have one.
You talk big. I talk short. Only one of us will be standing after the bell.
I know about your {strength}. Good, then. I have seen what it does to people who are careless.
You can be proud of your {strength}. Pride does not keep you upright.
You are cool. Fine. Good, then. Keep that until I am on the floor.
Calm answer. I will take it, and I will see if you keep it.
I could shout. I do not need to.
One fall, hot and fast. Hot and quick. Keep me down, and I will be surprised.
On the mat, I am not going anywhere until I say so.
Grounded is where you want me. It is not where you will keep me.
Stay on your feet if you can. It makes no difference to me.
That was an answer, barely warm. Now prove it.
Did you hear me? I asked a question. Answer it.
Fine, then. Let us get on with it.
I will fight until the bell goes, and I will not stop when it does.
Plain and straight: I am here to wrestle this one, and I am going all out.
Whatever happens, you will know where I stood.
Nothing is decided yet. We will see.
The rest of this talk is wasted. Go and warm up.
No. I cannot prove that. I can fight you in the ring, not prove a guess.
You want an example. I do not have one. Fine. Forget the charge.
Fine. Leave it. Bring your fight.
Good. No more heat from that. Bell.
Let them see what happens when you meet resistance. A speech won't do that.
I can show you what my wrestling is worth. The result will speak for itself.
Enough about the accusation. What can you show me in the ring?
Talk is cheap. What can the crowd actually judge when we wrestle?
My {strength}. You know what's coming. Stop me, then.
You've got an answer to my {strength}. Save it for the ring. I want to feel it, not hear it.
Sure. No sense calling a thing proven when it's still got to be done.
I'll give you that much. Put the rest to the test in the ring.
